item.title: February 2026 regulatory update: from passage to practice
item.description: Editor’s note: This monthly update covers regulatory developments across Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and Canada. Our aim: help regulators understand what is now live, why it matters, and what is coming. If you haven’t already, consider signing up for our monthly newsletter to stay abreast of the latest regulatory developments. February takes the big […]

item.title: Rethinking what it means to be a regulator
item.description: Veronica Taylor and Adam Slater on building regulatory professionalism and new ways of thinking about regulation.

item.title: AI governance in regulation: from hallucinations to accountability
item.description: AI governance in regulation is already being tested in hearings, licensing, and complaints. The question now is accountability.

item.title: March 2026 regulatory update: stress-testing new regimes
item.description: New cybersecurity mandates, AUSTRAC's biggest AML transition in a generation, and competition regulators retooling across three jurisdictions. Our monthly scan of what's live, what's coming, and what it means for regulators.

item.title: If AI cannot explain exam grades, it is not ready for enforcement
item.description: Ofqual says AI cannot mark high-stakes exams. The explainability problem now faces regulators using AI for fraud detection and supervision. A test case for regulatory AI capability.

item.title: When cyber security becomes product safety
item.description: Smart device rules in Australia, the UK, and EU say insecure IoT is a faulty product. This feature asks whether regulators are ready to enforce that idea.

item.title: The UK set an AI copyright deadline. It forgot to appoint an enforcer.
item.description: Parliament required answers on AI, copyright, and enforcement. Ministers delivered a delay. No UK body has been designated to police how AI systems use creative work – and the biggest models are trained abroad, beyond UK law's reach. A deep-dive into the enforcement gap, what the courts left unresolved, and three lessons for regulators everywhere.

item.title: The UK is about to massively expand cyber regulation. Its regulators aren't sure they're ready.
item.description: Ransomware hit NHS hospitals and wiped £300m off M&S's profits. Now Parliament is asking whether the agencies meant to police the UK's new cyber rules have the staff, systems, and data to do it.

item.title: When growth becomes the test: what merger control reveals about regulatory politics
item.description: Deals blocked globally fell by more than half in 2025. Governments are rewriting competition rules at speed – and in opposite directions. The accountability gap is the real story.

item.title: Cyber security as product safety: will it be enforced?
item.description: Insecure smart devices are now legally defective products in multiple jurisdictions. The harder question is whether regulators are equipped to enforce that shift.
